articles.body: Introducción de la aplicación Prisma permite examinar ventas desde diferentes dimensiones. El usuario puede pasar del año al mes o al día, seleccionar un país y separar ventas de devoluciones o ajustes. La pantalla combina indicadores, una tabla con subtotales y un gráfico de los grupos de mayor magnitud. El repositorio público incluye la preparación de datos, el código del cubo, las pruebas y los workflows. La aplicación se publica en GitHub Pages . La herramienta OLAP elegida es Perspective , distinta de Druid, Pinot, ClickHouse, Snowflake y DuckDB. El proyecto no utiliza AWS. Propósito y herramientas utilizadas La pregunta es cómo consultar el mismo conjunto de ventas desde distintas perspectivas y conservar totales consistentes.

articles.title: SMS Event Notifications: Retaining Delivery Evidence for Healthtech Contact Routing
articles.excerpt: For a healthtech contact form, the bill for SMS event notifications using common APIs includes sending messages, retrieving delivery evidence, storing that evidence, and investigating submissions that…
articles.body: For a healthtech contact form, the bill for SMS event notifications using common APIs includes sending messages, retrieving delivery evidence, storing that evidence, and investigating submissions that never reach the right support queue. In the storage component, repeated observations can dominate: an illustrative workload of 1,200 notifications a day, eight retained observations per notification, and 30 days of retention produces 288,000 records. TL;DR: Route the contact form into an application-owned support record first, then track its SMS notification separately. Retrieve event evidence by message ID, reconcile delivery status, and keep compact summaries longer than raw observations. A provider's acceptance of a notification doesn't establish that a support team owns the request.

articles.title: Why AI Agents Silently Break Unreal Engine 5.9 Meshes: Projective-Radiometric Null-Space Drift (and How to Catch It Before Save)
articles.excerpt: If you have connected Claude, Antigravity, or a custom MCP toolset to Unreal Engine 5.8 or 5.9 to iterate on characters, modular assemblies, lighting, or materials, you have probably seen this failure…
articles.body: If you have connected Claude, Antigravity, or a custom MCP toolset to Unreal Engine 5.8 or 5.9 to iterate on characters, modular assemblies, lighting, or materials, you have probably seen this failure mode: The agent takes a front-facing Lit viewport screenshot, declares the edit "clean and verified," saves the asset—and then you orbit the camera 90 degrees and find a 20 mm collar spike pointing straight down the original camera ray , a chalk-white SSS = 0 subsurface dropout hidden under painted albedo, or a 180° dorsal hair groom floating off the back of the neck. We call this Projective–Radiometric Null-Space Drift (ViewDrift) —and it isn't just a prompt issue. It is a linear-algebra and radiometry blind spot.

articles.title: How We Built a Zero-Pro-Bytes Split-Binary Desktop App in Python (Ed25519 + Cloudflare Workers KV + Native Cython .pyd)
articles.excerpt: When you ship a commercial Python desktop developer tool, standard single-file packaging (PyInstaller / Nuitka / cx_Freeze) has a well-known problem: anyone can unpack your installer in thirty seconds…
articles.body: When you ship a commercial Python desktop developer tool, standard single-file packaging ( PyInstaller / Nuitka / cx_Freeze ) has a well-known problem: anyone can unpack your installer in thirty seconds with pyinstxtractor and read every if is_pro: check in plain bytecode. While building Token Czar v2.0 (our local PreToolUse context-window and prompt-cache hygiene guard for Claude Code, Cursor, and Antigravity), we wanted two things that usually fight each other: A 100% free, clean, zero-telemetry Lite desktop app any developer can download and verify immediately. Literally zero Pro code bytes inside the free binary—so there is nothing to crack, patch, or decompile out of the free download.

articles.title: Onboarding Packet Assembly: Fill, Merge, and Sign in One Job
articles.excerpt: The constraint that changes this design is evidentiary: a media company must be able to show exactly which onboarding forms an employee signed, while still rebuilding the packet when Legal replaces on…
articles.body: The constraint that changes this design is evidentiary: a media company must be able to show exactly which onboarding forms an employee signed, while still rebuilding the packet when Legal replaces one page. TL;DR: fill and retain each source form, merge them in a declared order, sign the completed bundle once, and make the whole job idempotent per employee. Put those operations behind an application-owned contract. The contract stays fixed when the document or signature vendor changes. Do not flatten early merely because a PDF library exposes a convenient flag. First make flattening an acceptance test: fields must become non-editable without losing their appearance, signature validity, or required audit evidence.

articles.title: Understanding the Four-Engine Architecture Behind Physical AI and AIoT in Healthcare
articles.excerpt: Physical AI and AIoT provide an architectural approach to connecting healthcare infrastructure with intelligent operational systems. A practical implementation can be divided into four engines: Identi…
articles.body: Physical AI and AIoT provide an architectural approach to connecting healthcare infrastructure with intelligent operational systems. A practical implementation can be divided into four engines: Identification Engine: Identifies medical equipment, supplies, patients and other operational assets. Sensing Engine: Collects information from connected devices, sensors and monitoring systems. AI Decision Engine: Analyses collected information to identify patterns, exceptions and operational opportunities. Physical AI Action Engine: Supports authorized workflows and physical-world actions with appropriate safeguards and human oversight. This architecture can support applications such as medical asset tracking, equipment maintenance, specimen traceability and hospital workflow coordination.

articles.body: A pair of companies in Europe have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of developing weapons that can be dropped from orbit. Atmos, a space company known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle , will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project. "We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, said in a statement on Nov. 18. The system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies said that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration.

articles.title: Who turned the W upside down? Why Cassiopeia won't sit still
articles.excerpt: The queen in the northern night sky is supposedly one of the easiest constellations to recognize — you just look for a W. Or is that an M?
articles.body: Some constellations are like old friends. You know them well, they're always there, and they never seem to change. A case in point is Cassiopeia, the queen. Its beautiful name comes from Greek mythology — the mother of Andromeda — and its shape is said to represent a queen sitting on a throne. To a stargazer, Cassiopeia is best known as a prominent northern constellation shaped like the letter W. It's easy to find — look north, find five reasonably bright stars making a W, congratulate yourself on finding Cassiopeia and use it to get somewhere more interesting. It's so often a signpost, not a destination. But look north a few hours after dark this month, and you'll notice the W has gone.
